listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Saturday, November 28. Here is what matters today. Our lead story comes from Drop Site News. Michael Dodd and his family own a defense consulting company. Since Dodd joined the War Department as assistant secretary for critical technologies, clients of that company have won up to three and a half billion dollars in military contracts. The report raises questions about how officials' family business interests overlap with the agencies they serve. Now the front page. The San Francisco 49ers have ruled quarterback Brock Purdy out with an ankle injury. Coach Kyle Shanahan says Mac Jones will start against the Seahawks on Sunday. It will be Jones's first start since last season. In architecture technology, a company called Nomic is extending AI agents into CAD drafting and BIM. Its tools generate native CAD files and automate drawing revisions. They work directly inside Revit and AutoCAD. In Atlanta, a new robotaxi is on the road. Zoox, which is owned by Amazon, is operating in the northwest part of the city, near Atlantic Station, Woodward and Home Park. Rides are limited for now. In science, astronomers caught a nearby supernova in early November. They soon realized it was something special, and they are now scrambling to study it. Now the sections. In tech, Simon Willison had Claude Opus 5.5 build experimental plugins to test a new hook in datasette-charts. A trending Claude Code skill bundle aims at bug hunting. And Google says a new method reaches comparable model quality up to three times faster. In politics, The Lever says a bipartisan bill could fast-track pipelines, data centers and fossil fuel projects. NPR reports that advocates are looking to the Supreme Court over changes to asylum rules. In world news, three years of war in Sudan have left millions of children displaced and hungry. Eight people died in a Peruvian military helicopter crash. And French actor Gérard Depardieu has been ordered to stand trial for rape and sexual assault. In sports, the Rockets, now fourteen and five, host the 76ers, who are sixteen and four. In UFC news, coach Eugene Bareman says Carlos Ulberg and Navajo Stirling will not fight each other for the title. In Atlanta, Urbanize lists eighteen reasons to be thankful for the changing city. Oprah Winfrey and T.D. Jakes will appear at the HOPE Global Forums in December. In architecture, a bamboo yoga shala in Costa Rica draws on the wings of a glasswing butterfly. A semicircular house in Brazil faces both the sunset and the sea. In science and nature, NASA's NG-25 mission will carry a space crop production system to the space station. Aerial photos show Florida Bay recovering as Everglades restoration sends more water. And a deep-sea fish eaten in 1984 has now been named a new species. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: After Pentagon Official Took Office, His Family Firm’s Clients Won Up to $3.5 Billion in Military Contracts
lead.note: Drop Site News reports that Michael Dodd and his family own a defense consulting company. Since Dodd joined the War Department as assistant secretary for critical technologies, clients of that company have won up to $3.5 billion in military contracts. The summary does not say how the contracts were awarded or what role, if any, Dodd had in them, so the reporting is best read as a question about the connection rather than a finding. The story matters because it concerns who benefits from large defense spending and how officials' family business interests overlap with the agencies they serve. For a reader who follows domestic politics through independent outlets, it is the most substantive political item today, with a specific figure and a named official.
